title: BxRig
tagline: Your dev rig. Beautiful by default.

pages.title: Desktop
pages.intro: Hyprland with Noctalia is the BxRig desktop. KDE Plasma stays on your machine either way; it is only configured if you choose it.

questions.label: Which desktops should BxRig set up?
questions.help: KDE Plasma is never removed. Choosing Hyprland leaves it untouched.

options.label: Hyprland + Noctalia (recommended)
options.description: A fast tiling desktop with a polished shell. Keyboard-first, Mac-style Super keys. KDE Plasma is left as it is.

options.label: Both: Hyprland + Noctalia, and KDE Plasma with BxRig tiling
options.description: Configure both with the shared BxRig keys, and pick which one starts at login.

options.label: KDE Plasma with BxRig tiling only
options.description: Keep Plasma and add HyprKwin tiling on top. Toggle it any time with: bxrig tiling on|off.

questions.label: Which one starts when you log in?
questions.help: Sets the login screen's preselected session. You can still switch there.

options.label: Hyprland + Noctalia
options.description: The login screen preselects Hyprland.

options.label: KDE Plasma
options.description: The login screen preselects Plasma.

questions.label: How should windows behave in Hyprland?
questions.help: The default layout. Change it later in the menu (Appearance, Windows, Layout), or per workspace with Super+Shift+J.

options.label: Tiling (recommended)
options.description: Windows split the screen on their own, no overlapping. Hyprland's default layout, called dwindle.

options.label: Tiling with a master window
options.description: One big window on the left, the others stacked beside it.

options.label: Three columns
options.description: Windows sit in three even columns, the main one in the middle. Hyprland's master layout, centred.

options.label: Scrolling (carousel)
options.description: Windows sit in columns on a strip you scroll sideways, like niri.

options.label: One window at a time
options.description: Every window full size; switch between them with Alt+Tab or Super and the arrow keys.

options.label: Floating windows
options.description: Normal overlapping windows you move and resize, like macOS. Tiling stays one keypress away.

questions.label: How should windows behave in KDE Plasma?
questions.help: HyprKwin's layout for your workspaces. Each workspace can switch later with Meta+Shift+J.

options.label: Dwindle (recommended)
options.description: Each new window splits the focused tile in half, along its longer side.

options.label: Master
options.description: One large window beside a stack of the others.

options.label: Monocle
options.description: One window at a time, filling the workspace.

options.label: Scrolling
options.description: Windows form a horizontal strip of columns you move along.

options.label: Stage
options.description: One main window with live previews of the others beside it, like macOS Stage Manager.

questions.label: Plasma panels
questions.help: BxRig layout: a top status panel (launcher, workspaces, active window, clock, media, system vitals, tray, in rounded islands) and a bottom dock. Your current panels are backed up first and can be restored with: bxrig plasma panels undo.

options.label: BxRig layout (recommended)
options.description: Top status panel plus a bottom icons-only dock, styled with Panel Colorizer.

options.label: Keep my panels
options.description: Leave the Plasma panels exactly as they are.

questions.label: Weather in the top panel
questions.help: Adds the Weather Report widget before the media controls.

questions.label: Event Calendar with an agenda instead of the plain clock
questions.help: Installs Event Calendar (AUR); the plain Digital Clock is the default.

questions.label: Workspaces always shown
questions.help: Empty workspaces stay visible in the bar.

pages.title: Look
pages.intro: Light or dark, the dock, the bar position and the clock. The top bar layout, the app grid style and the color theme have a page of their own after this one.

questions.label: Dark or light

options.label: Dark
options.description: Catppuccin Frappe neutrals with BoxLang green and cyan.

options.label: Light
options.description: Catppuccin Latte neutrals with deeper greens.

options.label: Auto
options.description: Follows sunrise and sunset.

questions.help: The color theme you pick later brings its own dark or light unless you choose Auto here.

questions.label: Dock
questions.help: A dock of your apps at the bottom of the screen (Noctalia). Change it later: bxrig appearance dock on|off.

options.label: Top
options.description: Like macOS.

options.label: Bottom
options.description: Like Windows.

options.label: Left
options.description: A vertical bar on the left.

options.label: Right
options.description: A vertical bar on the right.

questions.label: World clock
questions.help: A globe before the clock (Nov 5 - 15:44). Click it for every time zone you follow.

questions.label: Which time zones
questions.help: Change them later: bxrig time world add|remove ZONE.

questions.label: Screensaver
questions.help: BXRIG art in the theme's colours on every monitor after a while idle, then the lock. Any key or mouse move closes it. Try it: bxrig screensaver preview.

options.label: After 2.5 minutes
options.description: The screen locks after 5 minutes.

options.label: After 5 minutes
options.description: The screen locks after 10 minutes.

options.label: After 10 minutes
options.description: The screen locks after 20 minutes.

options.label: Off
options.description: No screensaver; the screen still locks after 5 minutes.

pages.title: Top bar layout
pages.intro: Pick how much goes on your top bar. The arrow keys change the preview live. You can change it later in the Control Center (Look page).

questions.label: Top bar layout
questions.help: Each choice shows its bar. The dock is set on the Look page.

options.label: Minimal
options.description: Minimal: the fewest icons. Everything else is one click away in the logo menu and the control center. Change it later: bxrig appearance bar layout minimal.

options.label: Standard
options.description: Standard: the recommended bar, the one you get if you just press Enter. Change it later: bxrig appearance bar layout standard.

options.label: Dense
options.description: Dense: for developers with a wide screen; a small one hides some icons. Change it later: bxrig appearance bar layout dense.

questions.label: Dock
questions.help: On by default, at the bottom of the screen. The grid button comes first and opens all your apps.

pages.title: App grid style
pages.intro: Pick how the app grid looks. It lists every installed app with a search box. The arrow keys switch between the two styles.

questions.label: App grid style
questions.help: Same apps, same search. Only the look differs.

options.label: Launchpad grid
options.description: Big colored icon tiles on a soft rounded card, with a grid button first in the dock. Change it later: bxrig appearance appgrid launchpad.

options.label: Terminal-style grid
options.description: Small flat glyphs on a square card with key hints and monospace labels. Change it later: bxrig appearance appgrid terminal.

pages.title: Theme
pages.intro: Colors the shell, terminals, btop, Neovim, window borders and the lock screen, and sets the theme's own wallpaper. The arrow keys preview each theme and this wizard follows the highlighted one.

questions.label: Color theme
questions.help: Change it any time: bxrig theme set NAME, or the Themes page of the Control Center.

questions.help: Content follows your fingers, like macOS.

questions.label: Mac-style Super keys
questions.help: On: Super+Z S F T N O P R W L B I U and Super+Tab behave like Cmd. Off keeps the Traditional (Omarchy-like) keys. Super+C, V, X and A copy, paste, cut and select all either way.

questions.label: Which keyboard do you type on?
questions.help: On a PC keyboard the Mac keys swap Alt and Win, so Alt acts as Cmd. An Apple keyboard already has Cmd there.

options.label: PC keyboard (swap Alt and Win)
options.description: Alt acts as Cmd, Win as Option. The default for a PC.

options.label: Apple keyboard (no swap)
options.description: Cmd and Option are already where the Mac keys expect them.

questions.label: Input devices found
questions.help: Filled in from the system: which of Apple Magic and Logitech devices are paired or plugged in. Never asked.

questions.label: Input devices (Apple Magic, Logitech)
questions.help: Magic Mouse and Magic Trackpad work through the kernel. This installs the helpers around them: Solaar for Logitech (the Linux Logi Options+), libratbag and Piper for gaming mice, upower for batteries, trackpad swipes on Hyprland. Undo: bxrig input undo.

options.label: Detect and offer helpers (recommended)
options.description: Sets up helpers only for the Apple and Logitech devices found now; nothing when none is found.

options.label: None
options.description: No input helpers.

options.label: Apple Magic Mouse or Trackpad
options.description: Battery (upower) and, on Hyprland, trackpad swipes (libinput-gestures).

options.label: Logitech mouse or keyboard
options.description: Solaar: buttons, DPI, scroll and battery.

options.label: Apple and Logitech
options.description: Both sets of helpers.

questions.label: Night shift (warmer screen at sunset)
questions.help: Hyprland: wlsunset with your time zone's sunrise and sunset, no network lookup. Plasma: its own Night Light in automatic mode.

questions.label: Trackpad gestures
questions.help: Three-finger swipes switch workspaces and open the overview (libinput-gestures). Works with Apple Magic Trackpad over Bluetooth.

questions.label: AirPlay receiver
questions.help: Lets your iPhone or Mac cast to this machine (UxPlay).

questions.label: Hot corners
questions.help: Move the pointer into a corner to run an action. Change them later: bxrig hotcorners set top-left overview.

options.label: Docker

questions.label: Docker commands on Podman
questions.help: Installs podman-docker and podman-compose so `docker run` and `docker compose up` work on Podman.

questions.help: Local containers on 127.0.0.1, with generated passwords. Nothing starts unless you pick it. Manage them with: bxrig db

questions.label: Database passwords
questions.help: Generated for you, or one you choose. Applies to the databases you picked; the admin user name is fixed per database.

options.label: Generated (recommended)
options.description: A strong random password for each, kept in a private file. Show it any time with: bxrig db info ENGINE --show-password

options.label: My own password
options.description: You type it (twice, hidden) as each database starts. Databases with no password (Redis, Chroma, Qdrant, Weaviate, Couchbase) are not asked.

questions.label: Mail catcher
questions.help: A local inbox for the mail your apps send while you develop (Mailpit in a container, SMTP on 127.0.0.1:1025, inbox at http://127.0.0.1:8025). Mail is thrown away when it stops. Manage it with: bxrig mail

pages.title: NAS
pages.intro: Connect a network drive (Synology, TrueNAS or any SMB or NFS share) so BxRig can mount it, even automatically, and back up to it. Skip this page if you do not have one.

questions.label: I have a NAS to connect
questions.help: You can add more later with bxrig nas add.

questions.label: Name for it
questions.help: Lower case letters, digits and dashes.

questions.label: Address of the NAS
questions.help: Find it with: bxrig nas discover

options.label: SMB (Windows file sharing)
options.description: What Synology offers by default. Needs a user name and password.

options.label: NFS
options.description: No password; the NAS allows your computer's address.

questions.label: Share to use for backups
questions.help: The folder share on the NAS, as DSM shows it.

questions.label: Mount it by itself when something opens it
questions.help: A sleeping NAS never blocks your login. SMB needs a root-only credentials file for this; the setup tells you.

questions.label: Your password
questions.help: You type the NAS password in the terminal while the setup runs. It goes to your keyring, never into a file.

pages.title: Remote backups
pages.intro: Back up somewhere else too: another computer over SSH, an rclone remote (FTP, WebDAV, Dropbox and more) or the cloud. Access keys are typed in the terminal while the setup runs and go straight to your keyring.

options.label: Nowhere else
options.description: Only the NAS above, if you added one.

options.label: S3-compatible cloud
options.description: AWS, DigitalOcean Spaces, Wasabi, MinIO. Asks for the endpoint, the bucket and the access keys.

options.label: Backblaze B2
options.description: Asks for the bucket and the account keys.

options.label: Azure Blob Storage
options.description: Asks for the container and the account name and key.

options.label: Google Cloud Storage
options.description: Asks for the bucket, the project and a service account key file.

options.label: Another computer over SSH (SFTP)

options.label: An rclone remote (FTP and more)

options.label: A disk or folder

questions.label: Name for it
questions.help: Lower case letters, digits and dashes.

questions.label: Region

questions.label: Service account key file

pages.title: Backups
pages.intro: Three layers, any of them. BxRig keeps the passwords and keys in your keyring and shows a plan before it changes anything.

options.label: My BxRig setup

options.label: The whole system
options.description: Snapshots with snapper on Btrfs (one before and after every update), Timeshift on other filesystems.

options.label: My files

questions.label: Local models
questions.help: Run AI models on this machine, no cloud. Nothing is preselected.

options.label: Ollama
options.description: Run models from the command line; the usual backend for local agents.

options.label: LM Studio
options.description: Desktop app to find, download and chat with models.

options.label: Jan
options.description: Open source ChatGPT-style app that runs fully offline.

options.label: KoboldCpp
options.description: Single-file text generation for GGUF models, with a web UI.

options.label: GPT4All
options.description: Simple local chat app for open models.

questions.label: BxRig local AI
questions.help: BxRig runs models on this machine with llama.cpp, with OpenAI and Anthropic compatible APIs on 127.0.0.1:8089. It checks your hardware and picks models that fit. Later works too: bxrig ai setup.

options.label: Set it up now
options.description: Installs llama.cpp (CUDA on NVIDIA, ROCm on AMD, Vulkan or CPU otherwise) and downloads the picked models.

options.label: Later
options.description: Skip it; run bxrig ai setup or open the AI page of the Control Center when you want it.

questions.label: Models
questions.help: BxRig picks up to three chat models for your hardware (fastest, balanced, most capable) plus a small embedding model. Downloads run at the same time.

options.label: The balanced pick
options.description: One chat model, the best mix of quality and speed here.

options.label: All three picks
options.description: Fastest, balanced and most capable; switch between them any time.

questions.label: Tune for this machine
questions.help: Benchmarks each model for about a minute to find the best threads, batch size and flash attention here. Run it later with bxrig ai models tune.

questions.label: Boxy, your desktop assistant
questions.help: Boxy is an AI agent built with bx-agents that knows this machine: ask it how the battery is doing, to switch the theme, add a reminder or install an app. It runs on your local model, and anything it changes waits for your OK. Super+Period opens a chat with it. Later works too: bxrig ai agents setup.

options.label: Set it up now
options.description: Installs bx-agents for BoxLang, makes Boxy in ~/Agents/Boxy and starts it.

options.label: Later
options.description: Skip it; run bxrig ai agents install --yes and bxrig ai agents setup --yes when you want it.

questions.label: Agent skills
questions.help: Skills teach your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode) how to use BxRig, BoxLang and MatchBox. They are stored once in ~/.agents/skills and linked into each agent. Find more with: bxrig skills search TEXT (the skills.boxlang.io hub).

options.label: BxRig
options.description: How to use and change this machine (five small skills, shipped with BxRig).

options.label: BoxLang language
options.description: BoxLang fundamentals: syntax, scopes, control flow, types (from the skills.boxlang.io hub).

options.label: MatchBox
options.description: The MatchBox runtime: native binaries, targets, the MVM (from the skills.boxlang.io hub).

pages.title: Import
pages.intro: Bring your own dotfiles. This runs last, so your files win over BxRig's starter configs.

questions.label: Dotfiles repository (optional)
questions.help: A git URL or a local path. Leave empty to skip.

questions.label: How it works
questions.help: BxRig detects whether the repository uses chezmoi, yadm, stow or plain files. Nothing is replaced without asking: files you already have are listed, and each one is backed up first. Undo any time with: bxrig dotfiles undo.
